title: Dedicated capacity: burst headroom shortfall causing request queuing and customer escalations
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Summary: Multiple large Dedicated customers reported elevated 429/503 errors and multi-second queuing for inference calls during burst traffic windows on 2026-03-09 through 2026-03-10. This ticket tracks investigation, immediate mitigations, and a permanent fix for a race condition in the reserved-pool allocator that allowed burst headroom accounting to under-report available capacity. Symptoms: (1) allocator stalled when concurrent pool reconciliation and quota refill overlapped, (2) autoscaler did not request additional nodes because the allocator returned a transient zero headroom state, (3) fallback routing to smaller model variants was not triggered because the routing policy relies on allocator signals. Impact: customer-facing latency spikes, billing anomalies (queued requests), and escalations to support/SE. Goals: ship a patched allocator + integration tests, deploy hotfix to affected Dedicated clusters, add observability and safeguards (metrics, alerting, automated fallback), and draft a customer communication and postmortem.
root_cause: Race in reserved-pool allocator between ReconcilePools() and RefillBurstCredits(): when ReconcilePools removed an underutilized worker while RefillBurstCredits was computing headroom, the allocator could transiently report zero available burst slots. Autoscaler logic treats zero headroom as saturated and suppresses scale-up for a 60s cooldown, causing sustained under-provisioning under concurrent bursts.
mitigation_and_hotfixes: 1) Emergency: increased configured burst headroom on affected Dedicated clusters by +25% to reduce immediate queuing (applied 2026-03-10 22:40 UTC). 2) Manual orchestration run to force-scale reserve pools in two clusters (r-nyc-3, r-eu-2) to target size while hotfix prepared. 3) Hotfix: make allocator operations idempotent and add a small in-memory lock around ReconcilePools()/RefillBurstCredits to prevent inconsistent headroom calculations. 4) Temporarily reduced autoscaler cooldown from 60s to 20s for affected release to allow quicker recovery while root cause patch is validated.
short_term_rollback_plan: If hotfix causes regression, revert allocator change and restore previous config; re-run manual scale up and maintain increased burst headroom. Rollback steps documented in the release notes and runbook linked below.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests added for concurrent ReconcilePools/RefillBurstCredits sequences. Integration test simulating overlapping bursts with synthetic traffic harness. Canary rollout to 10% of Dedicated clusters (staggered across regions) with traffic throttling and real-time latency/call-queue metrics. Pre-deploy validation includes synthetic load at 2x normal burst rate for 15m.
deployment_plan: Canary: runtime-1.23.1-hotfix -> 10% clusters (2026-03-13 03:00 UTC). Monitor for 2 hours. If stable, progressive rollout to remaining Dedicated clusters over 8 hours. Update autoscaler cooldown to 30s post-rollout. Post-deploy: pause for 24h to collect telemetry before normalizing configs.
observability_changes: Added metrics: reserved_pool_headroom_gauge, allocator_reconcile_duration_ms, allocator_lock_contention_count, autoscaler_suppressed_scaleups_total. Added alert: reserved_pool_headroom_below_threshold for >30s and autoscaler_suppressed_scaleups_total increasing by >5 in 5m. Dashboard: Dedicated->Pools->Headroom heatmap.
customer_notifications: Drafted customer communication explaining cause and mitigation; targeted outreach to affected accounts + SE handoffs. Template saved to Confluence and support ticket replies prepared. Planned proactive email after full rollout with detailed postmortem summary.

follow_up_actions: 1) Merge hotfix and backport to supported runtime branches (runtime-1.22, runtime-1.23).
2) Add integration test to CI that runs a short burst overlap scenario on PRs touching allocator or autoscaler.
3) Update autoscaler policy to avoid suppressing scale-ups if headroom transitions from zero to positive within 30s.
4) Run a tabletop incident review with CS/Sales/SE and update customer-running-playbook.
5) Add a permanent dashboard tile for 'suppressed scale-ups' per cluster and weekly report for top 10 clusters.
6) Document manual scale-up runbook and automation to force-scale reserve pools when headroom anomalies detected.
notes: This ticket focuses on Dedicated reserved-pool headroom accounting. Related work on routing fallback policies is tracked separately. Ensure legal/comms reviews for customer messages if required.
